items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Later I made an album for Camden with a big band, led by Andy Gibson, a very good arranger.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about when you came over to make those first records. Did you have the freedom to say, to pick the artist and say all right, I want to do Coleman Hawkins? Did you then let him pick the rhythm section?

Well you have to — there’s give and take there. You say I want so-and-so. Then they’ll say well I want so-and-so. And you’ve got to keep good will on both sides. Later I made an album for Camden with a big band, led by Andy Gibson, a very good arranger. And what we wanted to do was make the whole side of the album one number, just big swing thing. And it was a band I guess of about fifteen pieces. And then this band has been in the profession for oh probably thirty years at that time, and they knew everything,…
When you got to the end of a take, was it your call to decide that you needed to do another?
